title: Reduce streaming token latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, KV cache, batching
author: Ava Singh
release_notes: Performance: Reduce streaming token generation latency across common serving paths by: tightening token flush cadence, improving token-loop scheduling and backpressure propagation, prioritizing small-kernel work, and KV-cache read deduplication. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers observed tail latency on streaming generation where single-token flush cadence and token-loop backpressure caused visible token gaps for low-latency use cases (chat UIs, real-time assistants). This PR consolidates several runtime techniques to reduce per-token latency without changing model outputs: 1) tighten flush cadence and make flush timer cooperative with backpressure, 2) refactor the token emission loop to avoid unnecessary syscalls and sleeps under light load, 3) propagate backpressure signals more directly to scheduling and batching layers to avoid head-of-line blocking, 4) kernel scheduling hinting to prefer small token kernels on the hot path, and 5) KV-cache read dedupe to avoid duplicate reads when multiple in-flight requests share prefixes.

Summary of changes (single-line commit-style summaries):
- refactor(token_loop): remove sleep-on-empty-loop; use event-driven wakeups and per-connection micro-timers
- perf(flush): introduce adaptive flush cadence with cooperative backpressure integration
- sched(kernel): add scheduling hints for small-kernel fast-path execution and prioritize sub-batches under latency SLOs
- kvcache: add in-flight read deduplication and read-through batching for shared prefixes
- batching: tweak continuous-batching heuristics to favor latency-sensitive requests when under target concurrency
- observability: add token_emit_latency and flush_timer_histogram metrics; add tracing spans for token-loop and kvcache reads

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/streaming/token_loop.rs (refactor, new micro-timer/event integration)
- runtime/streaming/flush.rs (adaptive cadence logic)
- runtime/scheduler/kernel_hints.rs (new hinting API + integration)
- runtime/kv_cache/reader.rs (in-flight dedupe + batching)
- runtime/batching/continuous.rs (heuristic adjustments)
- observability/metrics.rs (new metrics)
- tests/streaming_latency/*.rs (unit + integration sims)

Small illustrative snippets included in the diff: token_loop now uses a single eventfd for wakeups and replaces a periodic sleep: if (!has_pending_tokens) { wait_on_event(); } else { emit_tokens(); } Flush cadence moved from fixed 20ms to adaptive: flush_ms = min(max(3, observed_emit_interval * 0.9), 20) and the flush loop skips if downstream backpressure high. KV-cache read dedupe uses an in-flight map keyed by (model, prefix_hash) returning a shared future for concurrent readers.

Tests and CI: Added unit tests for flush adaptive bounds and KV-cache dedupe. Added integration simulation that measures token inter-arrival times under various QPS and sequence-length distributions. CI: build and rustfmt/lint passed; flaky e2e streaming test retried in CI then passed.

Review conversation (high level):
- Marcus Lee: "Can we get a short justification for the chosen adaptive bounds (3ms min)? Concerned about CPU overhead at extreme fanout."
- Author (Ava): "3ms was chosen based on latency vs CPU tradeoffs in our sims (see benches/flush_latency.md). We also gate the adaptive path behind a dynamic budget that disables sub-ms flushes when CPU budget is exhausted. Added comments and a budget metric (flush_budget_percent)."
- Priya Desai: "KV-cache in-flight dedupe looks good; please ensure TTL and memory accounting are tracked."
- Author: "Added metrics for in_flight_dedupe_count and attached mem_estimate to the in-flight entry; TTL respected via existing cache eviction hooks."
- Ethan Carter: "Suggest a small opt-in config flag for kernel hint aggressiveness so Dedicated customers can tune."
- Author: "Added runtime config flag kernel_hint_aggressiveness (default=balanced) and documented in config reference."
- Priya: "Approved after minor docs/observability additions."
- Marcus: "Approved."

Merge/cut notes: Merged via squash. PR closes ENG-2345 and relates to ENG-2410. No user-facing API change; release notes added. Post-merge rollout: feature gated via runtime flags and a gradual ramp on Dedicated; target rollout window scheduled for 2025-12-01 with monitoring of token_emit_latency P50/P95 and CPU budget metrics.

Observability and follow-ups: Added metrics and tracing to validate in-prod behavior. Follow-up items: 1) evaluate additional kernel micro-optimizations (ENG-2501), 2) extend dedupe to include partial-prefix sharing (ENG-2560), 3) gather production telemetry for 2 weeks and revisit adaptive thresholds.

CI summary: All checks passed after a single flaky e2e retry. Merge executed after approvals.

Merge method: squash and merge.

perf(flush): adaptive flush cadence with backpressure integration
sched(kernel): kernel hinting for small-token fast-path
kvcache: in-flight read dedupe and read-through batching
